title: Israeli election salience fuses security, judicial relations, unity and identity while social confidence deteriorates
source_unit: Jewish People Policy Institute, Israeli Society Index, September 2026
geography: Israel; Jewish-sector and Arab-sector adult respondents as described by JPPI

observations.period: September 2026; assessments of Israel and the world

denominator.unit: JPPI September Israeli Society Index respondents: 663 Jewish-sector and 206 Arab-sector respondents

israel_improving_continue.unit: percent of all Israelis saying Israel is improving and will continue to improve; 43% among Jewish Israelis

israel_deteriorating_continue.unit: percent of all Israelis saying Israel is deteriorating and will continue to deteriorate; 54% among Arab Israelis

world_deteriorating_continue.unit: percent saying the world is deteriorating and will continue to deteriorate

domestic_world_gap.value: Israelis express more confidence in Israel's ability to improve than in the world's ability, while Jewish-Arab disagreement is much larger on Israel than on the world

observations.method: JPPI monthly society index using Madad.com Jewish-sector panel and Afkar Research Arab-sector online/telephone sample; weighted according to voting patterns and religiosity.
observations.uncertainty: The public report does not provide a full probability-sample design, response rate or item-level confidence intervals; cross-sector estimates should not be treated as directly interchangeable without the source weighting context.
observations.subgroup: Israeli adults represented by Jewish-sector and Arab-sector survey frames, with ideology and religiosity breakdowns.
observations.counterinterpretation: Improvement and deterioration categories can coexist with uncertainty, political mobilization or conditional optimism; these perceptions do not measure objective security, economic output or social cohesion.

observations.period: September 2026; past-year social, economic and security evaluation

social_year_poor.unit: percent describing the past year as poor socially; 4% described it as good

economic_year_poor.unit: percent describing the past year as poor economically; down from 35%

security_year_poor.unit: percent describing the past year as poor in security terms

social_crisis_ideological_gap.value: social deterioration was concentrated among center and left Jewish respondents, with poor assessments rising to 86% in the center-left and 70% in the center

observations.method: JPPI repeated monthly item comparison for social, economic and security assessments.
observations.uncertainty: These are retrospective judgments, not harmonized objective measures of social, economic or security conditions; subgroup comparisons depend on the source sample and weighting.
observations.subgroup: All Israeli respondents with Jewish ideological breakdowns reported by JPPI.
observations.counterinterpretation: A negative social assessment can reflect polarization, salient conflict or institutional disagreement without indicating uniform decline in social interactions or services.

observations.period: September 2026; election salience and decisive issues

most_important_elections.unit: percent saying the coming elections will be the most important in the country's history

especially_important.unit: percent saying the coming elections will be especially important

security_decisive.unit: percent saying who can most effectively maintain security will be decisive in their vote

judicial_relations_unity.value: relations between government and judiciary and unity follow security among decisive issues, with issue priorities diverging by ideology and Jewish/Arab identity

observations.method: JPPI election-attitudes module fielded in the September 1–3, 2026 index wave.
observations.uncertainty: Election importance and decisive issues are stated intentions, not turnout, vote choice, policy delivery or post-election legitimacy outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Israeli adults with reported Jewish ideological and Arab-sector comparisons.
observations.counterinterpretation: High election salience can reflect perceived stakes without increasing participation, and issue ranking does not establish which policy would satisfy voters.

observations.period: September 2026; identity, conflict attribution and education legitimacy

denominator.unit: JPPI Israeli Society Index respondents, with item-specific Jewish and Arab bases

gaza_perimeter_rejected_jewish.unit: percent of Jewish Israelis rejecting withdrawal from a Gaza security perimeter under any circumstances

full_occupation_support_jewish.unit: percent of Jewish Israelis generally agreeing with full occupation and IDF administration of Gaza for several years

antisemitism_policy_connection.value: 34% of Israelis said the rise in antisemitism is to a great extent because of Israeli policy, while 36% said not at all

education_not_good.unit: percent describing Israel's education system as not good, up from 32% in 2024

education_curriculum_contest.value: Jewish studies and civics divide curriculum priorities across religiosity and Jewish-Arab identity

observations.method: JPPI conflict, identity, antisemitism-attribution and education modules; items are separate and should not be pooled as one attitude scale.
observations.uncertainty: The report measures perceptions and normative preferences; it does not establish conflict conduct, antisemitism prevalence, educational quality, causal polarization or future policy behavior.
observations.subgroup: Israeli adults, with Jewish/Arab, ideological and religiosity breakdowns.
observations.counterinterpretation: Strong security preferences can coexist with concern about social decline or education; disagreement over attribution does not imply absence of shared institutions or future compromise.

related_sources.claim: JPPI Israeli Society Index programme and institutional context.

boundary: This record adds a geopolitical-cultural legitimacy route: security, judicial relations, unity, identity, conflict attribution and education are interpreted together as election stakes, while Jewish-Arab, ideological and religiosity differences remain central. It uses a weighted monthly panel and mixed Jewish/Arab survey frames, not a probability sample with fully disclosed uncertainty; it does not establish objective conditions, causality, turnout, policy delivery, conflict outcomes or durable cohesion.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The JPPI September 2026 Israeli Society Index page was reviewed for field dates, sample frames, domestic/world outlook, social/economic/security assessments, election salience, decisive issues, Gaza preferences, antisemitism attribution and education-system judgments.
